item.title: Week 1: New Orleans > Houston > Austin > Dallas > San Antonio
item.description:
Week 1: New Orleans > Houston > Austin > Dallas > San Antonio

A great way to kick off the fall tour, the band is tight and the bbq was good in the lone star state.

I finally got to make my pilgrimage to @collingsguitars HQ in Austin, and I truly believe you can’t get a better American made guitar than what they’re building there. I don’t own one yet, but I will soon. I’m happy to report that @tylerlyle left with a beautiful new Collings OM that he played that night for a special one off acoustic version of ”Brooklyn”

San Antonio tomorrow then we start pushing west for the next round of shows. Come out and see us! @themidnightofficial

Show Photos By: @josenaviazegada 📸

item.title: Rehearsals are wrapped, and @themidnightofficial tour starts today in New Orleans at Civic Theatre.
item.description:
Rehearsals are wrapped, and @themidnightofficial tour starts today in New Orleans at Civic Theatre.

This rig has never sounded better, in fact I don’t think I’ve ever had better live guitar tone than I do right now, and I couldn’t be happier. Thanks as always to @xacttone for getting the rack sorted and to @dvdby13 for building the best amps out there (aside from Two Rock)

Shoutout to @hamishdickinson for this IEM mix which is pretty great.

Check the dates and come see us if we’re coming through your town sometime in the next 6 weeks.

See yall out there.

item.title: I have the actual Logic session from the infamous @daddarioandco string demo last week that so many people think is AI generated. I’m going to do a l...
item.description:
I have the actual Logic session from the infamous @daddarioandco string demo last week that so many people think is AI generated. I’m going to do a longer video about this, but TLDR… I don’t think generative AI was used to make this track.

I’m someone who is staunchly against the use of Gen AI tools like @sunomusic for any part of the artistic process of writing and producing music, at best I think it’s a crutch for lazy or impatient musicians who are looking for a shortcut, and at worst it’s a slop machine, trained on stolen work that is actively harming those of us who make music for a living and the people who love music made by real people. If you’re a musician, writer, producer, content creator or anyone else in our space using or promoting Suno or other Gen AI tools I think you’re part of the problem and you need to seriously rethink why you make music in the first place.

With that said, I have been skeptical from the start of this whole debacle that @daddarioandco would have made the choice to use Gen AI tools to produce a demo for a new product, in my limited experience with them over the years as a player and content creator I’ve found them to be a company that cares about their users and their products. It just doesn’t make sense to me that a company that sells strings, sticks, drum heads etc. would take part in a system that has the potential to undermine their own customer base, but that’s just my opinion.

This isn’t definite proof that Gen AI wasn’t used for this demo, but the fact that I can disable the (monumental) stack of plugins and get to a DI guitar track here that sounds normal to my ears is pretty strong evidence, but you can decide that for yourself.

Like I said, I’m working on a longer video about this which should be out soon.

item.title: For the last few weeks I’ve been getting in the practice of making some kind of sketch every morning on a piece of gear, and I figured I should start...
item.description:
For the last few weeks I’ve been getting in the practice of making some kind of sketch every morning on a piece of gear, and I figured I should start recording & posting them.

I’ve had the Analog Rytm mkII for a few years now, but never really have dug too deep into it and I wanted to change that so this morning I loaded up some breaks and ended up with this. I’m still very new to the Drum and Bass thing, so any helpful tips from actual producers out there would be grateful appreciated.

This machine is an impressive piece of kit, when I bought it from @perfect_circuit I found it to be a little overwhelming, but that was me not knowing enough about sampling, drum programming and synthesis. Now that I’ve learned a lot more I’m having a blast with this groove box, and find it to be pretty inspiring like all of the @weareelektron boxes I’ve played.

And yes, my screen is going bad (it just started happening this morning) I’ve already emailed support.

I’m going to try and make a habit of recording and posting the stuff I’m working on, as a way to help push me to develop and finish ideas, rather than just scrolling endlessly through samples and presets.

#drumandbassmusic #elektron #sampler

item.title: It feels weird to admit, but I basically haven’t touched a guitar since I’ve been home from tour. I’m still learning and working on music pretty mu...
item.description:
It feels weird to admit, but I basically haven’t touched a guitar since I’ve been home from tour. I’m still learning and working on music pretty much every day though. I’ve struggled with identity quite a bit, specifically as a musician. Imposter syndrome is something very real and I still deal with it on a daily basis, and it’s held me back in a lot of ways.

For a long time I’ve held myself back from trying new things because I didn’t think I would fit in, or maybe I wasn’t good enough or “legit” enough to go in a certain direction musically, so I would subconsciously guilt trip myself into “staying in my lane” as a guitarist. This was definitely a contributing factor to a biblical level of burnout a few years ago that I’m still trying to manage to this day, and part of the way I manage it is to let myself go down whatever rabbit hole I feel pulled towards that day, week, month…whatever

Maybe this is the early stages of my forthcoming mid-life crisis, but I’ve fallen deep into the Drum and Bass / Jungle thing and I absolutely fucking love it. A few years ago I probably wouldn’t have let myself learn about this type of music, let alone attempt to make it, I would have told myself something like “that won’t help your guitar playing” or “the audience doesn’t want to hear that” but now, I couldn’t give less of a shit and I think that’s progress?

I dunno, I think it’s cool. I suck at it, and that’s ok… this stuff takes time to really learn and that’s what I love about music, you’ll never stop learning.
